name: Gina Raffaelli
fact: At the first Congress meeting of the year, on 27 August 1996, she moved that the Student Government Association adopt the budget Treasurer Steve Roadcap had just presented, after an earlier motion by Rick Malek to table the vote was defeated; David Apple seconded her motion and the budget was accepted. She was recorded absent from the meetings of 1 October and 8 October 1996.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 27 Aug 1996; absences recorded 1 Oct and 8 Oct 1996

name: Amy Wilson
fact: She applied for the vacant Senior Off-Campus representative seat and spoke to Congress on 25 February 1997 about why she wanted to join; Stephanie Cosby moved to seat her by acclamation, Heather Rogers seconded, and the motion passed. She was recorded absent from the meetings of 1, 8, 15 and 22 April 1997.

name: Jason Wong
fact: Congress filled the two open Sophomore Off-Campus seats by unanimous consent on 29 October 1996, seating him alongside Callie Varner. The roll thereafter records him absent from most meetings of the rest of the term, including 13 and 23 November and 3 December 1996 and 21 and 28 January, 4, 11 and 18 February and 4 and 11 March 1997.

name: Jeff Oliver
fact: Congress filled the open Junior Off-Campus seats by unanimous consent on 3 September 1996, seating him with Keith Coffman, Andy Gailor and Sara Haswell. On 3 December 1996 he voted for the resolution on housing refunds, which carried 22 to 17 on a roll-call vote. On 4 February 1997 Vice President Carlene Lodmell nominated him to the Judicial Council; Rick Malek moved to accept the nomination, Andy Gailor seconded, and the motion passed.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 3 Sep 1996, 3 Dec 1996 and 4 Feb 1997

name: Joe Mathis
fact: He was one of ten members who voted on 29 October 1996 to reconsider Jason Cole as Vice Chair for Student Affairs, a motion defeated 19 to 10. On 3 December 1996 Public Relations Director Shawna Whartenby gave him a special award for serving on the Residence Hall Task Force, and he voted that night for the housing refunds resolution, which passed 22 to 17. He voted against tabling the by-laws revision on 18 February 1997 and for the residence hall privatization study on 22 April 1997.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 29 Oct 1996 and 3 Dec 1996

name: Tracy Guthrie
fact: She attended the meeting of 4 February 1997 as a visitor and was seated the same night, when Congress filled the vacant Freshman Council and Sophomore Off-Campus positions by unanimous consent with Rachel Hendricks and Guthrie. On 18 February 1997 she voted in favour of tabling Bill 97-1-S, the by-laws revision, so the administration could review it; the motion to table carried 21 to 16.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 4 Feb 1997 and 18 Feb 1997

name: Travis Mayo
fact: On 29 October 1996 he was among the ten members who voted to reconsider Jason Cole as Vice Chair for Student Affairs, a motion defeated 19 to 10. On 3 December 1996 he voted for the housing refunds resolution, which passed 22 to 17 on a roll-call vote. He was recorded absent on 24 September, 8 October and 23 November 1996 and on 28 January and 4 February 1997.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 29 Oct 1996 and 3 Dec 1996

name: Jason Chilton
fact: He wrote Resolution 98-15-F, which asked that the SGA advisor checklist be printed in the fall and spring schedule bulletins. On 17 November 1998 he spoke for it on second reading and offered a friendly amendment correcting a word in the first whereas clause; Leslie Bedo moved to accept it as amended and Congress approved it. He and Bedo also authored Bill 98-11-F, on orientation for new members, and both spoke for it when it passed on second reading on 8 December 1998. He was recorded absent on 10 February 1999.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 17 Nov 1998 and 8 Dec 1998

name: Bill Brown
fact: On 1 December 1998 he spoke against Bill 98-10-F, which would have allocated funds to the Kappa Alpha Order fraternity, in a long floor fight that also drew Rick Malek, Jason Nemes, Dwight Campbell and Mitchell Bailey; after a failed amendment to raise the sum from 250 dollars, the bill was defeated 20 to 22. He was recorded absent on 3 November 1998, 10 February 1999 and 23 March 1999.

name: Michael Richardson
fact: Congress voted to accept him as an At-Large member on 30 January 2001, and he was sworn in that evening with Anna Coats and Dana Lockhart; Joe Morel was sworn in as a Justice at the same meeting. The minutes of 10 April 2001 carry a Mike Richardson in the list under the Keown Award heading.

name: David Logan
fact: Congress approved him and he was sworn in as a member on 16 January 2001, together with Natalie Taylor, Stacey Taylor and Robin Fulkerson. The same meeting postponed Resolution 00-5-F to 23 January, passed Resolution 00-6-F, and swore in Mark Rawlings as Vice President of Finance.

name: Natalie Taylor
fact: Congress approved her and she was sworn in as a member on 16 January 2001, in the same group as Stacey Taylor, Robin Fulkerson and David Logan. That meeting also confirmed Mark Rawlings as Vice President of Finance and Holly Skidmore as Public Relations Committee chair.

name: Stacey Taylor
fact: Congress approved her and she was sworn in as a member on 16 January 2001, in the same group as Natalie Taylor, Robin Fulkerson and David Logan. That meeting also confirmed Mark Rawlings as Vice President of Finance and Holly Skidmore as Public Relations Committee chair.

name: Margaret Haydon
fact: On 6 February 2001 Congress moved and approved accepting her and Krista Harris as At-Large members, and both were sworn in that evening. The same meeting passed Bill 00-1-S, the SGA Teaser Award, on second reading and gave Bill 00-2-S, a bulletin board purchase, its first reading.

name: Stephen Martin
fact: He was sworn in as an At-Large Congress member on 6 March 2001, at the meeting that approved Resolution 01-4-S and the election codes and gave first readings to Bill 01-7-S on the Spring Bash, Bill 01-8-S on a faculty appreciation day and Resolution 01-5-S on matching fund fee reallocation.

name: Amy Joyce
fact: She was sworn in as an At-Large member of Congress on 29 January 2002, at the meeting that gave first readings to Bill 02-1-S, a constitutional amendment, and Bill 02-2-S on the Sun Belt tournament trip, and confirmed Dwight Campbell as parliamentarian.

name: Annie Henning
fact: She was sworn in as an At-Large member of Congress on 5 February 2002 together with Eddie Schwab. She was still in Congress the following year: the minutes of 5 February 2003 list her among the affirmative speakers in the debate on the president's nominees, a vote Congress ended up tabling for two weeks.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 5 Feb 2002; later, minutes of 5 Feb 2003

name: Amy Lee
fact: She was sworn in as an At-Large member of Congress on 12 February 2002, in a group of four with Charlie Walker, Kyle Gott and James Dunn. The same meeting gave first readings to Resolution 02-2-S on the freshman seminar, Bill 02-4-S on SGA unity and Bill 02-5-S, a bylaws amendment.

name: James Dunn
fact: He was sworn in as an At-Large member of Congress on 12 February 2002, in a group of four with Amy Lee, Charlie Walker and Kyle Gott. The same meeting gave first readings to Resolution 02-2-S on the freshman seminar, Bill 02-4-S on SGA unity and Bill 02-5-S, a bylaws amendment.

name: Kyle Gott
fact: He was sworn in as an At-Large member of Congress on 12 February 2002, with Amy Lee, Charlie Walker and James Dunn. He was still active the next year: on 5 February 2003 he spoke in opposition during the debate on the president's nominees, and on 18 March 2003 he was one of three members who argued that the Apollo Night showcase request should go through the organisational aid process instead.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 12 Feb 2002; later, minutes of 5 Feb and 18 Mar 2003

name: Craig Johnson
fact: He was sworn in as an At-Large member of Congress on 26 February 2002 together with Dustin Hayes, at the meeting that passed Bill 02-12-S on a campus clean-up and adopted the 2002 election codes.

name: Dustin Hayes
fact: He was sworn in as an At-Large member of Congress on 26 February 2002 together with Craig Johnson, at the meeting that passed Bill 02-12-S on a campus clean-up and adopted the 2002 election codes.

name: Dustin Brumett
fact: He was sworn in as an At-Large member of Congress on 5 March 2002, in a group of five with Brandon Copeland, Sam Stinson, Mason Shields and Blain Fentress. That meeting saw Bill 02-1-S, the constitutional amendment, fail for want of a two-thirds majority and then be tabled for reconsideration, while the banner, chambers sign and outdoor furniture bills passed.

name: Mason Shields
fact: He was sworn in as an At-Large member of Congress on 5 March 2002, in a group of five with Brandon Copeland, Sam Stinson, Blain Fentress and Dustin Brumett. That meeting saw Bill 02-1-S, the constitutional amendment, fail for want of a two-thirds majority and then be tabled for reconsideration, while the banner, chambers sign and outdoor furniture bills passed.

name: LaJohna Brown
fact: Congress approved her as Vice-Chair of the Academic Affairs committee on 18 September 2001, alongside Patti Johnson for Public Relations and Ross Pruitt for Legislative Research, at the meeting that debated and approved the 2001-02 SGA budget. On 9 April 2002 she was one of ten members nominated for the Committee award.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 18 Sep 2001 and 9 Apr 2002

name: Kristin Hartley
fact: President John Bradley appointed her chair of the Senior Recognition committee at the first meeting of the year, 27 August 2002, and Congress approved the committee and coordinator appointments unanimously on a motion by Sam Stinson. She had been nominated for the Committee award the previous April, and on 4 March 2003 she moved the adoption of Resolution 03-03-S on one-stop accounting, which passed unanimously after the bookstore director spoke for it.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 27 Aug 2002 and 4 Mar 2003

name: John Adams
fact: He came to Associated Students from Fern Creek and sat on the Rules and Elections Committee in 1967-68, one of three members named on the officers roster the president's office filed that year, which noted two more places were still to be appointed. The Herald had reported his election as freshman class president in October 1966, a result settled only after four recounts, and in April 1968 it reported that he had been elected chairman at the Southern Universities Student Government Association conference.

src.label: UA3/3/1 Associated Student Government Officers 1967-68; Herald 46:3, 13 Oct 1966; Herald 47:26, 4 Apr 1968

name: Thelma Lee
fact: She sat on the Student Activities Committee of Associated Students in 1967-68 with Dennis Jaffee, Carol Bass and campus representative at large Keith Petrie, on the officers roster filed with the president's office. The roster gives her home as Vine Grove, Kentucky. The same document shows the association's judicial and financial committees had not yet been formed when it was drawn up.

name: Sandra Tonjes
fact: She sat on the Rules and Elections Committee of Associated Students in 1967-68 with John Adams and Paul Gerard, on the officers roster filed with the president's office, which recorded that two further places on that committee were still to be appointed at the start of the next year. The roster gives her home as Bowling Green, Ohio.

name: Dana Lockhart
fact: Congress moved and approved her admission as an At-Large member on 30 January 2001, and she was sworn in that evening alongside Anna Coats and Michael Richardson, at the meeting that dissolved the Special Events Committee and created an ad hoc committee on online elections. She stayed with SGA for three more years: on 9 April 2002 she was nominated for both the Committee and the Stewart awards, on 27 August 2002 she was sworn in to the Judicial Council, and through 2002-03 she delivered the Judicial Council and University Senate reports to Congress, including the ruling on the secretary reporting on workload and the Council's review of the election codes. The Herald covered her twice as a candidate for SGA office, on 4 April 2002 under the headline that SGA could not be as elitist as it had been, and on 20 March 2003 under a headline about wanting a comfortable atmosphere.

src.label: SGA Congress minutes, 30 Jan 2001; minutes of 27 Aug and 24 Sep 2002; Herald 77:49, 4 Apr 2002 and Herald 78:47, 20 Mar 2003

name: Kyle Key
fact: He won the freshman class presidency in the SGA freshman elections of autumn 1992. Administrative Vice President Susan Mitchell read the results to Congress on 29 September 1992: Key as president, Greg Edmonds as vice president, and Jill Howard, Margaret Carter, Jennifer Raffaelli, Darron Brawner and William Zorn as freshman representatives. He was recorded absent on 17 November 1992 and on 12 and 19 January, 9 February and 2 March 1993.

name: Jill Howard
fact: She was elected a freshman representative in the SGA freshman elections of autumn 1992. Administrative Vice President Susan Mitchell reported the results to Congress on 29 September 1992, naming Kyle Key as freshman president, Greg Edmonds as vice president, and Howard with Margaret Carter, Jennifer Raffaelli, Darron Brawner and William Zorn as representatives. The roll records her absent on 20 October and 1 December 1992 and on 2 and 9 February, 9 March and 13 April 1993.

name: Darron Brawner
fact: He was elected a freshman representative in the SGA freshman elections of autumn 1992, reported to Congress by Administrative Vice President Susan Mitchell on 29 September 1992 along with freshman president Kyle Key, vice president Greg Edmonds and fellow representatives Jill Howard, Margaret Carter, Jennifer Raffaelli and William Zorn. The roll records him absent on 27 October 1992 and at five meetings between 26 January and 23 February 1993.

name: William Zorn
fact: He was elected a freshman representative in the SGA freshman elections of autumn 1992, reported to Congress on 29 September 1992 with freshman president Kyle Key, vice president Greg Edmonds and representatives Jill Howard, Margaret Carter, Jennifer Raffaelli and Darron Brawner. During the same year the Herald printed a piece by him criticising university president Thomas Meredith, headed as another big blunder, in the issue of 18 February 1993.

name: Jenny Stelmach
fact: Joe Tinsley moved her approval as Senior Representative on 26 January 1993, in the same slate as Laura Nunn, Jeff Carlisle and David Serafini, at the meeting that gave first readings to a bill for a student phone in the Preston Center, a bill for a fax machine in the SGA office and a resolution for a copy machine in Garrett. On 23 February 1993 she gave the Grievance Committee report in place of chairperson Dawn Dillard, telling Congress that billboards had been put up for students to write their grievances on.

name: Laura Nunn
fact: Joe Tinsley moved her approval as Junior Representative on 26 January 1993, in the same slate as Jenny Stelmach, Jeff Carlisle and David Serafini; the motion passed. The same meeting approved three new committee chairs and gave first readings to Bill 93-1-S for a student phone in the Preston Center, Bill 93-2-S for a fax machine in the SGA office and Resolution 93-1-S for a copy machine in Garrett. She was recorded absent on 13 April 1993.

name: Jeff Carlisle
fact: Joe Tinsley moved his approval as Representative at Large on 26 January 1993, in the same slate as Jenny Stelmach, Laura Nunn and David Serafini; the motion passed. On 30 March 1993 he was one of two members named as moving that the reading of the minutes be suspended, a motion that failed, so the minutes were read out and approved. He was recorded absent on 23 March, 6 April and 13 April 1993.

name: Susanne Jeffiers
fact: Congress approved her as Education Representative on 2 February 1993, with Kendra Welch as Sophomore Representative and Eddie Myers as sophomore vice president. The same meeting passed the fax machine bill after motions to table and to amend it both failed, passed the Garrett copy machine resolution unanimously on second reading, and gave a first reading to Resolution 93-2-S on a study day preceding exam week. She was recorded absent on 9 March 1993.

name: Kendra Welch
fact: Congress approved her as Sophomore Representative on 2 February 1993, alongside Susanne Jeffiers as Education Representative and Eddie Myers as sophomore vice president. That meeting also passed the bill for a fax machine in the SGA office and, unanimously, the resolution for a copy machine in Garrett. The roll records her absent at most meetings after that, including 2, 9 and 23 March, 30 March, 6 April and 13 April 1993.

name: Tim Sturm
fact: Congress approved him as Sophomore Representative on 9 February 1993, in a group of five with Lisa Rosa, Thomas Lally, Elizabeth Fauver and Andrea Cailles. The same meeting amended and then unanimously passed Resolution 93-2-S on a study day before exam week, and gave a first reading to Bill 93-3-S establishing a recognised SGA philanthropy. He was recorded absent on 30 March and 13 April 1993.

name: Lisa Rosa
fact: Congress approved her as Junior Representative on 9 February 1993, in a group of five with Tim Sturm, Thomas Lally, Elizabeth Fauver and Andrea Cailles. The same meeting amended and unanimously passed the resolution for a study day before exam week and gave a first reading to the bill establishing an SGA philanthropy. She was recorded absent on 9 March and 6 April 1993.

name: Shawn Pinkston
fact: Congress approved him as Representative at Large on 16 February 1993, together with Michael Bessette as non-traditional representative, at the meeting that passed Bill 93-3-S establishing a recognised SGA philanthropy unanimously on second reading and gave a first reading to Bill 93-4-S on organisational aid recipients. He was recorded absent at five of the last six meetings of the term. The Herald covered him as an SGA candidate on 12 April 1994 under a headline saying he would not raise fees.

name: Kim Mann
fact: Congress approved her as Representative at Large on 23 February 1993, at the meeting that passed Bill 93-4-S on organisational aid recipients on second reading, voted to make Head Start the association's philanthropy, and gave a first reading to Resolution 93-3-S on an advocate programme for handicapped students. The roll records her absent at every meeting from 23 March to 13 April 1993.

name: Jim Lee
fact: He was a member of SGA Congress in the spring semester of 1993. What the record holds of him is the attendance roll, which names him absent at every regular meeting from 26 January to 13 April 1993, eleven in all. Congress enforced attendance that year through the Judicial Council: on 9 February 1993 the secretary told committee chairs to send members with absences before Emily Morgan and the Council.

src.label: SGA minutes, 26 Jan 1993 to 13 Apr 1993; enforcement noted 9 Feb 1993

name: Jeff Duncan
fact: He was a member of SGA Congress from the start of the 1992-93 year. The record of him is the attendance roll, which names him absent from thirteen meetings between 15 September 1992 and 9 February 1993, beginning with the meeting where president Joe Rains reported his presentation to Regent Earl Fischer on what it was like to be a student at Western. He was not among the members who resigned in the round of absence letters the secretary reported on 2 February 1993.

name: Molly Schreiner
fact: She was a member of SGA Congress in the spring of 1993. The surviving record of her is the attendance roll, which names her absent on 16 February 1993, the night Congress passed the bill establishing a recognised SGA philanthropy and gave a first reading to the bill on organisational aid recipients, and again on 23 March 1993. Congress was enforcing attendance that term: the secretary reported on 2 February that letters to members with excessive absences had produced four resignations.

name: Ray Ezell
fact: He sat in SGA Congress through the autumn of 1992 under president Joe Rains, and the attendance roll records him absent only twice, on 22 September and 20 October 1992. In the second week of that semester the Herald printed a piece by him arguing the university should say residence hall rather than dorm, in the issue of 27 August 1992.

name: Lena S. Garner
fact: She served as a senior off-campus representative on the Fall 1994 membership list, which enters her as Lena S. Garner; the minutes call her Lena Sweeten and the minutes of 29 March 1994 give the full form, Lena Sweeten-Garner, when she gave the Public Relations report on flyers for the coming election and Dialogue Day. Congress approved her as coordinator of committees on 6 September 1994. Treasurer Brandon Rucker thanked her on 25 October for helping interview the organisational aid applicants, on 31 January 1995 committee chairs were told to meet with her, and on 17 January 1995 she asked members to think of a topic for SGA's first student forum.

src.label: SGA minutes, 29 Mar 1994, 6 Sep and 25 Oct 1994, 17 and 31 Jan 1995

name: Jason C. Hays
fact: He was a sophomore off-campus representative on the SGA membership list for the autumn of 1994. At the first meeting of the year, 30 August 1994, chairperson Bonnie Newton named him vice chairperson of Student Affairs, and on 17 January 1995 Congress approved him as vice chair of the Student Athletic committee under Jason Young. In April 1995 he stood with Young for the executive, the two running for president and vice president; the ticket is listed in the minutes of 4 April, and the results announced on 18 April gave the offices to Tara Higdon and Jeff Yan. The Herald of 6 April 1995 ran a student government item headed that Jason Young and Jason Hays backed New Level, the shorthand for president Thomas Meredith's Moving to a New Level proposal to raise admission standards, which Congress discussed through that spring.

src.label: SGA minutes, 30 Aug 1994, 17 Jan, 21 Feb, 4 Apr and 18 Apr 1995; Herald 70:50, 6 Apr 1995

name: Jayson R. Richardson
fact: He was a sophomore off-campus representative on the Fall 1994 membership list. The attendance roll names him absent at eight of the first nine meetings, from 30 August to 25 October 1994, the stretch in which Congress passed the resolution to repaint the informational sign, approved the 1994-95 budget and passed Bill 94-1-F on homecoming candidates. He was present from 1 November 1994 onward.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 30 Aug to 1 Nov 1994

name: Phillip J. Eleson
fact: He was one of eight junior off-campus representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list; the minutes also spell him Elesan. The attendance roll records him absent on 20 September 1994 and then through the late-autumn run of meetings, 15, 22 and 29 November and 6 December 1994 and 17 January 1995, which covered reserved parking, sponsoring a family for Christmas, the Angel Tree and the creed monument. He attended the rest.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 15 Nov 1994 to 17 Jan 1995

name: Amanda K. Thurmond
fact: She was one of eight junior off-campus representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list. The attendance roll names her absent at the first four meetings of the year, 30 August and 6, 13 and 20 September 1994, which took in the constitutional review, the approval of the 1994-95 budget and the voter registration drive, and records her present from 27 September onward.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 30 Aug to 27 Sep 1994

name: Heather Renee Meenach
fact: She was one of six senior off-campus representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list. The attendance roll records her absent only twice all year, on 13 and 20 September 1994, at the meetings on the constitutional review and the phonathon and on the voter registration drive; she was present at every other meeting of 1994-95.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 13 and 20 Sep 1994

name: Ernie Chen
fact: He was one of eight sophomore off-campus representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list. The attendance roll names him absent at ten of the first eleven meetings of the year, from 30 August to 8 November 1994, present only on 18 October, and then present from 15 November onward, through the meetings on tuition increases and the campus violence task force, reserved parking and the creed monument.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 30 Aug to 15 Nov 1994

name: Sharman R. Mooney
fact: She was one of eight junior off-campus representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list. The attendance roll records her absent at ten of the first eleven meetings of the year, from 30 August to 8 November 1994, present only on 13 September, and then present from 15 November 1994 to the end of the term, through the meetings on reserved parking, the Angel Tree, the creed monument and the spring election.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 30 Aug to 15 Nov 1994

name: Rod P. Sherrill
fact: He was a sophomore off-campus representative on the Fall 1994 membership list, which spells him Rod P. Sherrill; the minutes write him as Rob Sherrill and Rob Sherill. The attendance roll records an unbroken run of twelve absences from 11 October 1994 to 31 January 1995, covering the child care grants debate, homecoming elections, the tuition increase, the Angel Tree and the creed monument. The roll names only absentees, and his name does not appear in it again after that date.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 11 Oct 1994 to 31 Jan 1995

name: Troy A. Nunn
fact: He was one of eight junior off-campus representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list. The attendance roll names him absent at three of the first four meetings of the year, on 30 August and 6 and 20 September 1994, and at none thereafter, so he sat through the whole of the rest of the term, from the approval of the 1994-95 budget in September to the announcement of the election results on 18 April 1995.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 30 Aug to 20 Sep 1994

name: John W. Taylor
fact: He was one of three non-traditional representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list, with James E. Parvin and Julie A. Martin McCay. The attendance roll names him absent only twice in the year, at the opening meeting of 30 August 1994 and on 14 February 1995, so the record has him present for almost every meeting of 1994-95, including the constitutional review, the tuition increase debate and the spring elections.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 30 Aug 1994 and 14 Feb 1995

name: Julie A. Martin McCay
fact: She was one of three non-traditional representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list, with James E. Parvin and John W. Taylor; the minutes enter her as Julie Martin. The attendance roll names her absent at the first four meetings of the year, 30 August and 6, 13 and 20 September 1994, and at none after that, so she sat through the rest of the term.

src.label: SGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994; SGA minutes, 30 Aug to 20 Sep 1994

name: James E. Parvin
fact: He was one of three non-traditional representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list, with John W. Taylor and Julie A. Martin McCay. He is not named once in the attendance roll of any of the twenty-five meetings of 1994-95, and since the roll lists only absentees that is a complete attendance record for the year. The Herald printed two letters from a Jim Parvin about support for Hilltopper basketball, on 16 February and 30 March 1995.

name: Jill C. Reading
fact: She was one of eight junior off-campus representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list. The attendance roll names her absent at the first three meetings of the year, 30 August and 6 and 13 September 1994, at which Congress approved the Judicial Council, passed the resolution to repaint the informational sign and adopted the 1994-95 budget, and she is not in the roll after that.

name: Jason F. Gerst
fact: He was a sophomore off-campus representative on the Fall 1994 membership list, and the attendance roll names him absent on 13 and 27 September 1994 and 14 February and 18 April 1995. He came back the following year: on 12 September 1995 Congress accepted him by acclamation as a junior off-campus representative, the minutes describing him as an Evansville junior, and he was recorded absent on 31 October 1995.

name: Charles J. Young
fact: He was one of six senior off-campus representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list, sitting with Angelo J. Rodriguez, Edward Myers, Annemarie Maxwell, Lena S. Garner and Heather Renee Meenach. His name is not in the attendance roll of any of the twenty-five meetings of 1994-95, and because the roll names only absentees, the record gives him a full year of attendance. Congress that year approved a resolution to repaint the informational sign, passed Bill 94-1-F on homecoming candidates and voted through Resolution 94-11-F asking that instructors give students a grade before the end of the withdrawal period.

name: Erik L. Turner
fact: He was one of eight sophomore off-campus representatives on the Fall 1994 membership list.
